title: See when a metaclass builds a class
sources: Python 3.14 Language Reference, data model: metaclasses, preparing class namespace, creating class object and class decorators; reviewed 2026-10-03
masterChecklist: Descriptors, decorators, metaclasses, class creation hooks — advanced/internals
whyItMatters: Some frameworks change classes at definition time. A tiny metaclass experiment shows that this happens before you create any instances—and why a simpler decorator or subclass hook is preferable for ordinary rules.
simpleExplanation: An ordinary class is itself an object made by the metaclass type. A custom metaclass can subclass type and override __new__(mcls, name, bases, namespace) to inspect or alter class creation. This receives the class name, base classes and body namespace, then should delegate to type.__new__ through super().__new__. In the standard class-creation path, type.__new__ also arranges descriptor __set_name__ calls and parent __init_subclass__ calls; decorators are applied after the class object exists. A custom metaclass is powerful but can conflict with bases using incompatible metaclasses. Use a simple function, class decorator or __init_subclass__ when those express the rule.
mentalModel: The metaclass is the factory that makes a class blueprint; __init__ later sets up each instance made from that blueprint. A decorator labels the completed blueprint afterward.
outcomes: Distinguish class creation from instance construction.
Trace a tiny metaclass __new__ call and a class decorator.
Delegate to type.__new__ so normal class machinery still runs.
Name a case where simpler hooks are preferable and recognize metaclass-conflict risk.

realWorldExample.scenario: A reporting framework wants a definition-time check that every report type declares a title.
realWorldExample.riskWithoutSetup: A silent metaclass can surprise maintainers, and composing it with another framework's metaclass may fail.
realWorldExample.professionalApproach: Prefer __init_subclass__ for a simple inherited title rule. Use a custom metaclass only for framework-level construction needs, with documented order and tests.

explanation: TraceMeta.__new__ runs while Python constructs StudyReport, before any StudyReport instance exists.
The decorator receives the completed class and then adds a label.
StudyReport.__init__ runs only after StudyReport() creates an instance.
Delegating to super().__new__ retains normal type-based construction; this is a learning trace, not a recommendation to install TraceMeta across an app.
workedExample.safeExperiment: Remove @labelled and predict the events. Do not modify type.__new__ or create dynamic classes from untrusted strings.

procedure: First decide whether a decorator or __init_subclass__ would state the requirement more clearly.
For learning, subclass type and record when __new__ receives the class name and namespace.
Delegate to super().__new__ so Python's class construction continues normally.
Apply a decorator and compare its event position with metaclass creation.
Create one instance and compare when __init__ runs; keep the example isolated from production design.

commonMistakes.why: They run at different phases: class definition versus instance creation.
commonMistakes.avoid: Trace events before and after calling the class.

commonMistakes.mistake: Replacing type.__new__ behavior without delegating or handling __classcell__.
commonMistakes.why: Normal descriptor, subclass and zero-argument super machinery can break.
commonMistakes.avoid: Delegate to super().__new__ for an ordinary custom metaclass.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using a metaclass for a one-off label.
commonMistakes.why: It adds complexity and possible metaclass conflicts for a trivial change.
commonMistakes.avoid: Use a class decorator or explicit attribute instead.

lab.title: Trace class definition before instance initialization
lab.safety: In-memory event strings only; no dynamic execution, plugins, files or network.
guidedSteps: Append meta:StudyReport inside TraceMeta.__new__ and delegate with super().__new__.
Make labelled append decorator:StudyReport, set label and return the class.
Print events before constructing an instance.
Construct one instance and print events again.
Print type(StudyReport).__name__ and compare it with the instance's class name.
checks: Before instantiation, the metaclass and decorator events are present, but no instance:init.
The class metatype name prints TraceMeta.
The decorator returns the class and metaclass delegates to type.
hints: The class decorator receives cls after class construction.
lab.solutionExplanation: The trace separates class-object construction, decorator application and instance initialization in that order.
challenges: Find the bug if labelled forgets to return cls.
Experiment: define another class with the same metaclass and observe that class creation is traced before any instance is made.

projectConnection.milestone: Document class-definition-time behavior in the report registration design and use the simpler subclass hook unless a framework-level factory is justified.
projectConnection.definitionOfDone: A test proves the metaclass/decorator/instance event order, and the design note explains why production uses or avoids the metaclass.

assessment.question: When does a custom metaclass __new__ run?
assessment.answer: When the class object is created during class definition.
assessment.explanation: It runs before any instance is constructed.

assessment.question: When is a class decorator applied in the normal class-creation path?
assessment.answer: After the class object has been created.
assessment.explanation: The decorator receives that class and its return value is bound to the class name.

assessment.question: Why call super().__new__ in this metaclass?
assessment.answer: To delegate ordinary class construction to type's machinery.
assessment.explanation: Skipping it can break important class-creation hooks and behavior.
